summary.text: Alan Currie is standing for Family First in Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The party says he has run small businesses for over four decades and has helped others start their own. It also says he is a family man with an interest in the country's Christian heritage.

priorities.text: Support for families
Helping small businesses grow
Sound economic management and responsible government
Private enterprise and personal responsibility

summary.text: Bailey McCracken is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian state election. He is a boilermaker and calls himself a unionist and a socialist. His campaign page centres on opposing AUKUS and the US alliance, building public housing and raising taxes on billionaires, banks and corporations.

priorities.text: As an anti-imperialist, I stand for smashing the US–Australia alliance.
AUKUS must be ripped up.
Taking over empty homes and idle land for public housing, built by a publicly owned builder run by its workers
Higher taxes on billionaires, the big banks and corporations to pay for rebuilding industry
Support for unionists opposing new AUKUS bases

summary.text: Jill Nambu is the Greens candidate for Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian state election. She lives in Hampton Park, works in the disability sector and sits on a school council. She volunteers as an English tutor for newly arrived migrants and helps run migrant playgroups, and has campaigned over the redevelopment of the former Cranbourne Golf Course, a waste transfer station planned for Hampton Park and a data centre proposal at Clyde North.

prior_roles.role: Volunteer English tutor for recently arrived migrants

priorities.text: I want to represent the voice of local residents who are working hard
Relief from the rising cost of living
Protecting and growing local parks, green space and the tree canopy
Better public infrastructure and services that are easy to reach
A state government that is transparent and held to account

summary.text: Lydia Denker is the Libertarian candidate for Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian state election. Born in Germany, she moved to Melbourne with her family at the age of eight and had a pop music career, releasing the 2004 single "One Perfect Day" and reaching the top 24 of Australian Idol's fourth season in 2006. She founded Homeschool Academy Australia, an education business, and her party says her experience of looking for schooling outside the mainstream for her son shaped her focus on education choice.

occupation.text: Founder of Homeschool Academy Australia, an education business

priorities.text: More freedom for parents to choose how their children are educated
Lower taxes and less government interference, with fairer conditions for small businesses
Safer streets, justice for victims and prison for serious offenders
Personal responsibility and free speech

summary.text: Norliah Peterson is the Liberal candidate for Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian state election. She teaches music, runs her own music school and also works at a local school, and has lived in Narre Warren for over two decades. After her son died of meningococcal B disease, she campaigned for free access to the vaccine, including a petition presented to federal Parliament; the Liberal Party credits her campaign with the vaccine becoming free for 16-year-olds in Victoria.

occupation.text: Music teacher and music school owner

priorities.text: Cost-of-living relief for local families and small businesses
Lower taxes and less red tape so local businesses can grow
Less crime and a safer Victoria
Stronger health care

sources.title: Narre Warren South: VIC electorate, candidates, results, ABC News

summary.text: Scott Watson is standing as an independent for Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian state election. A Lynbrook resident of more than 20 years, he has been president of the Lynbrook Residents Association and was part of the community campaign against the proposed Hampton Park waste transfer station. He served with Victoria Police in the 1990s, later worked in human services and local government, and these days operates Dr Hotdog, a food stand at BP Lynbrook. His campaign asks voters to elect an independent for a single term and make the parties compete for the seat again in 2030.

occupation.text: Small business owner (Dr Hotdog food stand, BP Lynbrook)

prior_roles.role: Victoria Police (1990s), including the Police in Schools program
Human services, including drug and alcohol policy and service delivery

prior_roles.note: Neither source says when he held the role or whether he still does.

priorities.text: Stop governing to be popular. Govern for the future.
All I need is one term.
Electing an independent for four years so that every party has to compete for Narre Warren South again in 2030
Judging policies on the evidence and on their merits, whichever party puts them forward
Answers on how the Hampton Park waste transfer station proposal got as far as it did before it was rejected

summary.text: Stefan Koomen is Labor's candidate for Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian state election. He won a place on Casey's council in 2024 and, when he stood aside to run for state parliament, was in a second straight term as mayor. He holds a commerce degree with majors in accounting and economics, and his past jobs include truck driving, managing a business and advising government.

occupation.text: Former Mayor of Casey; earlier a truck driver, business manager and government adviser

prior_roles.note: The ABC says he stepped down to run for parliament but doesn't say whether he left the council or only the mayoralty.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says he was elected to the council in 2024; no source gives his ward or the label he stood under.

priorities.text: Easing cost-of-living pressure, more affordable housing and safer communities, which his party page lists as his first priorities
Investment in local health services and schools
Careful spending of public money
Keeping Doveton Pool open; as mayor he also opposed a waste transfer station planned for Hampton Park

summary.text: Trevor Hammond is One Nation's candidate for Narre Warren South at the 2026 Victorian state election. A self-employed tradesman, he has run a business in the area for over 43 years and has spent decades in the building industry. He stood for One Nation in the federal seat of Holt in 2025, and his party says he helped raise local awareness of a proposed hazardous-waste transfer station.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC names him as One Nation's candidate for Holt but doesn't give the result.

priorities.text: If I say I'm going to fight for something, I fight.
Tougher action on youth crime and graffiti
More coal and gas baseload power to cut electricity bills, with renewables only where they can compete without subsidies
Lower living costs and more affordable housing
Spending on local roads, children's playgrounds and things for teenagers to do
